html:
The Cathedral of Santa Maria la Menor in Santo Domingo, built between 1514 and 1541, is the oldest cathedral in the Americas. The Pope made it the first cathedral of the New World.

It mixes late Gothic vaults with a plateresque Renaissance front, in coral limestone. For centuries it was the seat of the archbishop who led the Church in the Spanish Caribbean.

The bones said to be those of Christopher Columbus lay here until 1992, when they were moved to the Columbus Lighthouse; Seville also claims them. The cathedral is part of the colonial city of Santo Domingo, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, near the first university.
